On Windows, MaiCord 0.5.x through 0.7.x install this update from Settings > Updates. If you're still on 0.4.0, follow the one-time manual steps in the [0.5.0 release notes](https://github.com/maj113/MaiCord/releases/tag/v0.5.0). On Linux, the installer and tarball installs and the AppImage update from Settings > Updates, packages through your package manager, and the musl AppImage through AppImageUpdate.

### Highlights

- **Tabs in the title bar.** Settings > Appearance > Layout > "Show tabs in the title bar" is off by default; with it off, the title bar is unchanged.
  - Pin a channel or DM with "+", Ctrl+T, "Open in new tab" in its menu, or a middle-click on its row. Up to 16 tabs; when they don't fit they shrink to icons, then the rest move behind "...". Drag to reorder; right-click for Close, Close others and Close to the right. The server's name sits beside the window buttons.
  - A channel tab shows a dot while the channel is unread. Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab switch, Ctrl+W closes, Ctrl+1 to 9 jump. Tabs come back after a restart. A version without tabs cannot read them and starts with its last-channel memory empty.
  - Choose "Open in new tab" on a picture, GIF, video, audio file or voice message (its menu, an embed's, or the image viewer's button) to give it a page of its own, up to 8. Spoiler and explicit-content blocks apply as they do for Save. Opening the same item again switches to its tab.
  - A video or track keeps playing, with sound, while you work in another tab, and its tab shows it. Video pages have transport, seek, volume, full screen, and Space, arrows, M and F. A playlist page has a YouTube Music-style queue with thumbnails, titles and durations beside the player (below it on narrow windows); click a track to jump to it.
  - Screen readers get an "Open tabs" list, the unread state, the player and the queue.
- **Go Live.** Share a screen or window, with its sound, from the voice card or the call bar. On Windows, pick an application or a whole screen; on Linux, the desktop's share dialog opens.
  - It is encoded on the GPU and end-to-end encrypted, at Discord's resolutions and frame rates up to your Nitro's or the server's boost tier, or at any of them with "Unlock all qualities" in the stream options (off by default; only clients check these limits). You get stream mode and quality settings, mute stream audio, your own tile with its viewer list, and a stream menu.
  - MaiCord's own sound is never shared. Sharing sound needs Windows 10 version 2004 or later, or PipeWire on Linux, which also needs xdg-desktop-portal; the packages recommend libpipewire, and MaiCord runs without it.
- **Account and server settings.** My Account (username, e-mail, phone, password, authenticator app, SMS, backup codes, disable and delete), Devices, Data and Privacy, Connected Apps, and blocked and ignored lists.
  - Security keys can be registered, on Windows and on Linux, and a first two-factor method shows its backup codes.
  - Server Profile gets a banner upload, and Server Tag, Server Template, Access (join applications), Enable Community, Integrations (command permissions, AutoMod, webhooks and more) are new.
  - Settings > Accessibility follows Discord's: a live preview, UI density, chat text size, zoom (Ctrl+= / Ctrl+- / Ctrl+0), saturation, role colour dots, underlined links and reduced motion that follows the system. Streamer Mode hides invites and personal information, has its own keybind, can turn itself on while OBS or XSplit runs (opt-in) and, on Windows, keeps the window out of screen captures; a band above the window shows while it is on.
  - Settings > Keybinds lists your custom keybinds with Edit and Delete. `/tts` messages are sent as text-to-speech and read like Discord's, at the Accessibility speech rate.
- **Profiles, friends and chat.** Profiles are laid out like Discord's, with Board, Activity, Mutual Friends and Mutual Servers, connected accounts and one activity card everywhere. Home gets a "Find or start a conversation" bar, Online, All, Pending and Add Friend tabs, and Message Requests with Requests and Spam.
  - Type `@game` to mention a game from Discord's catalogue; it shows as a chip and opens the game's profile. Clicking an attachment's ALT badge opens its description. The typing indicator reads like Discord's.
  - A colour picker with an eyedropper serves the theme editor, Roles and text forms. Dialogs, segmented controls and tooltips animate in and out.
- **Uploads.** The free upload limit is 20 MiB, as Discord raised it, and MaiCord no longer refuses a file by its own count: Discord decides, and a file that is too large says so and names the limit.
- **Removed.** Spotify sign-in is gone (it saved a login nothing used) and a saved one is deleted at startup. Spotify embeds, activity links and the profile connection are unchanged.
- **Performance.** The Windows MaiCord.exe is 6.45 MB and the Linux program 6.46 MB, both under 6.5 MB with all of the above.
  - Voice, Go Live audio, voice messages and the soundboard use MaiCord's own Opus encoder and decoder instead of a libopus fork: 26 to 32% less encoding time and 13 to 26% less decoding time, with the same output on Windows and Linux. It passes the Opus conformance vectors (RFC 8251).
  - JSON decodes up to 14% faster on text full of escapes, and member list updates 1 to 4% faster.
  - Scrolling, switching channels, the member list and theme changes use the same main-thread CPU time as 0.7.0 or slightly less, with the same memory; nothing wakes while the window is hidden.
  - Deciding what a frame has to redraw takes 29% less time.
  - Scrolling the emoji picker uses about a third of the GPU time it did (7 to 10% down to about 3% at 1440p and 125%), with no frame over 16.7 ms: colour emoji draw only the layers that reach each part of the glyph, and a full glyph atlas makes room by evicting the least recently used rows instead of starting over.
  - Text rasterizes in 20% less GPU time; WebM (VP8) video decodes with 27% less GPU time in prediction and 6% less in the loop filter.
  - On Linux, CRC32 is 17 times faster from 1 KB up.
  - Smaller wins in voice level checks and the AAC decoder's start (same output) and in animation curves (within a hundred-thousandth of the exact curve).
- **Requirements.** The README's CPU line now names POPCNT for Linux as for Windows; both clients already needed it.
- **For developers.** A Linux test-only build takes 25 s instead of 52 s.
- **Fixes.**
  - Some WebP avatars showed as a grey circle because they failed to decode; they decode now. A GIF whose transparent colour lies outside its palette now plays instead of failing.
  - Emoji suggestions after ":" rank by how you use emoji from the first message, not only after the picker was opened. Flag, custom and Unicode rows line up their names.
  - Mention pills and composer chips centre on their text; descenders no longer touch the border.
  - Selecting text in a channel stopped at the message it started in. A drag now runs on over the following or earlier messages, in a group and across authors, and scrolls the chat when it reaches the top or bottom edge; Ctrl+C copies every selected message in order, a line each, with the author lines it passes.
  - Settings text could vanish after a failed rebuild; it redraws on the next frame.
  - The Accessibility preview card shows two messages with your avatar, and the AMOLED theme uses Discord's midnight colours.
  - The server tag page shows the saved badge as Discord's image.
  - Screen readers get the heading and status on every sign-in screen; before, some states (password shown, code ready, cooldown) had none.
  - A crash when adding members to an integration.
  - A server could turn into a blank, unavailable icon if MaiCord received it while you were in one of its voice channels (at startup, after a reconnect, or with your call still open on another device); it now loads.
  - With a gradient theme, the taskbar and tray icon was Discord's blurple; it takes the theme's accent now, and MaiCord's violet when the gradient is grey.
  - On Windows Server 2025, a memory lock shortfall could fail a secure allocation; it is handled.
